There are 10 University of California (UC) campuses in the United States [d1][d2][d8]. The official University of California website lists "10 campuses," and the UC Office of the President document similarly references "10 campuses" [d1][d8]. Wikipedia confirms the system "is composed of its ten campuses at Berkeley, Davis, Irvine, Los Angeles, Merced, Riverside, San Diego, San Francisco, Santa..." [d2]. Of these 10, nine campuses offer undergraduate and graduate programs, while UC San Francisco (UCSF) is dedicated solely to graduate and professional education in the health sciences [d3][d5]. Some sources refer to "nine campuses" when specifically discussing undergraduate-admitting schools, but the total count of UC campuses is 10 [d4][d6][d7].
